item.title: Foraging niche segregation among woodpeckers in the oak-pine forest of Kumaon Himalaya, Uttarakhand, India: Woodpecker Foraging Niche Segregation
item.description: Understanding how species that share the same habitat coexist can reveal how niche segregation helps reduce competition and structure communities. item.title: Local knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions of ecosystem services and disservices provided by the Painted Stork &lt;Mycteria leucocephala&gt; Pennant, 1769 (Aves: Ciconiidae) in northern India: insights for conservation
item.description: Understanding the knowledge, attitudes and perceptions of the local communities towards the target species before implementing any awareness-based programmes is essential for the success and long-term protection of the species. item.title: A note on the Petal-less Caper &lt;Maerua apetala&gt; (B.Heyne ex Roth) Jacobs (Capparaceae)
item.description: The Petal-less Caper Maerua apetala (B.Heyne ex Roth) Jacobs (= Capparis apetala B.Heyne ex Roth) is a large-canopied but short dry evergreen tree, endemic to southeastern India. Though several publications on this species are available, none of them have reported its girth at breast height. Further, all publications reported it as deciduous tree with height ranging 4–10 m. item.title: Record of &lt;Euploea mulciber&gt; (Cramer, [1777]) (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae) in Delhi, India: evidence of range extension in a restored urban ecosystem
item.description: This study documents the first records of the Striped Blue Crow butterfly, Euploea mulciber, in Delhi, India, observed within the Aravalli Biodiversity Park in 2013, 2018, and 2022. Previously unrecorded in the region despite extensive butterfly surveys, these sightings suggest a potential range extension, possibly facilitated by the park’s restored urban green space, which provides host plants and nectar sources. item.title: Hump-nosed Pit Viper &lt;Hypnale hypnale&gt; feeding on an Allapalli Skink Eutropis allapallensis in Karwar, India
item.description: We report a probable first case of in situ field observation of a wild Hump-nosed Pit Viper Hypnale hypnale hunting and feeding. This is based on a direct observation involving an Allapalli Skink Eutropis allapallensis that occurred on 23 May 2024, at 2200 h in Karwar, India. The entire event lasted for 6 m 40 s, while the skink became immobile, eventually died out of envenomation in just 40 s after fang-contact.

item.description: Freshwater palaemonid prawns of Nagaland is studied based on the collections made during different surveys from 1998 to 2022 by various survey teams of Zoological Survey of India, Kolkata. item.title: Species composition of butterflies associated with nectar feeding on <Libidibia coriaria> (Jacq.) Schltdl (Magnoliopsida: Fabales: Fabaceae)
item.description: Butterflies are vital bioindicators and pollinators, with their diversity often reflecting ecosystem health. This study assessed the species richness of butterflies visiting Libidibia coriaria during its flowering season within the Kerala Agricultural University campus. A total of 41 butterfly species were recorded, representing approximately 29.5% of the 139 butterfly species previously documented from the campus. item.title: First camera-trap evidence of a ferret badger <Melogale> sp. (Mammalia: Carnivora: Mustelidae) from the community forests of Manipur, India
item.description: Individuals of Melogale sp. were photographed on multiple occasions through camera traps deployed in the community forest of Godha Village under Phungyar Sub-Division of Kamjong District, in Manipur, India. The species were photographed from fragmented forest patches along the village’s vicinity. item.title: First photographic record of Smooth-coated Otter <Lutrogale perspicillata> from the canals in Upper Ganga Ramsar Site, Uttar Pradesh, India
item.description: Smooth-coated Otter Lutrogale perspicillata is one of the three species of otters found in India. Photographs from the Lower Ganga Canal confirmed the presence of the species in the Ganga River in January of 2021 and 2023. This is the first confirmed record of a Smooth-coated Otter from the canal network of the middle stretch of the Ganga River. item.title: Identification of wildlife crime hotspots in Punjab, India via kernel density estimation analysis
item.description: Punjab is a predominantly agrarian state and among the least forested in India. It remains underrepresented in w ildlife crime research. item.title: New distribution records and taxonomic studies of ascomycetous fungi <Xylaria> and <Daldinia> (Ascomycota: Xylariales: Xylariaceae) in Karnataka, India
item.description: The family Xylariaceae represents a diverse assemblage of ascomycetous fungi, widely recognised for their prolific production of secondary metabolites with potent bioactive properties, including antimicrobial, anticancer, and immunomodulatory compounds. A mycological survey was conducted from June 2023 to August 2024 across various ecological niches in Karnataka, India, to document the diversity of Xylariaceae. item.title: Diversity and distribution pattern of geometrid moths (Insecta: Lepidoptera: Geometridae) along the altitudinal gradient, Kumaun Himalaya, India
item.description: Altitudinal gradients are frequently used to study Lepidoptera diversity. The study site, situated in the Munsiari Subdivision of Pithoragarh District, Kumaun Himalaya, was divided into transects along the altitudinal gradient, each 200 m wide, spanning elevations from 1,200–4,000 m. item.title: New record of two natricine snakes, <Hebius gilhodesi> (Wall, 1925) and <Herpetoreas davidi> Nguyen et al., 2024 (Reptilia: Squamata: Colubridae), from India
item.description: Two natricine snakes, Hebius gilhodesi and Herpetoreas davidi, are reported for the first time from India based on mitochondrial DNA and morphological data. This study extends the northwestern-most distribution of H. gilhodesi by 107 km and H. davidi by 577 km, both of which were thus far known only from adjacent Myanmar. Additionally, a detailed description of the hemipenial morphology of H. gilhodesi is provided.

item.title: Composition and ecological guild structure of birds at Chaudhary Devi Lal University campus, Haryana, India
item.description: Documentation of avian diversity is an effective method to monitor the quality of a habitat, along with long-term effects of habitat fragmentation, developmental activities, and urbanization. In the current investigation, the avifauna diversity of the university campus was examined from December 2022 to December 2024. item.title: Predicting the potential habitat of <Tragopan blythii> (Jerdon, 1870) (Aves: Galliformes: Phasianidae) in Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary of Arunachal Pradesh, India
item.description: The Blyth’s Tragopan Tragopan blythii is a medium-sized pheasant endemic to the eastern Himalaya and is classified as ‘Vulnerable’.
